text:
ops-bot: PAGING: Elevated backend request queue + sustained worker backpressure detected in us-west-2 inference cluster. Throughput degraded ~40% for hosted text-gen & embeddings. Triggering on-call.

alex: oncall here, seeing p95 token latency creeping up and throughput drop. Pool saturation on gpu-pool-7, many 500s from batch-worker.

michael: noticing a spike in large-batch submissions from a few API keys, may be batching abuse. Throttling rules didn't kick in because new route name.

laura: good catch. I'm toggling the burst policy to limit concurrent large batches and will pause the autoscaler for gpu-pool-7 to avoid noisy scale churn.

alex: do that, and also add a temporary routing rule to steer new requests to fallback-model-small where appropriate. We'll keep gen-quality slightly lower but restore throughput.

jamie: I'm on infra to restart the batch-worker fleet on pool-7 after we set limits. Restart sequence ETA ~8 minutes.

ops-bot: Incident severity: high (production impact). Customers impacted: subset of hosted API users -- heavy batch/embeddings workloads. Suggested mitigations: throttle large batches, route to fallback model, restart workers, flush KV cache.

alex: I'll prepare a short status page note and a customer notification snippet for CS to send. Keep me posted on restart results.

michael: results from throttling: large-batch q-length down 60% in 90s. Some p95 improvement. Still seeing a small residual queue.

jamie: restart complete on batch-worker group. Services reporting healthy but token throughput still ~10% below baseline. Tracking slow ramp due to warmup/kv-cache misses.

laura: flushing prefix cache for pool-7 to accelerate warmup. Also enabling short-lived cache priming for common prefixes.

michael: after flush + priming, throughput at ~95% baseline. p95 latency back to acceptable band. Looks like mitigation successful.

ops-bot: STATUS CHANGE: Mitigations applied (throttle large batches, fallback routing, worker restart, cache priming). Partial recovery reported. Continue monitoring for residual errors.

alex: great. ETA to full recovery: 10-20 minutes while caches warm and throughput normalizes.

laura: I'll keep autoscale paused for 30 minutes to avoid thrash, then handoff to next oncall.

michael: CS / account teams, here's a draft customer notification you can use. Please personalize if needed.

cs-team-bot: posting suggested snippet below.

--- CUSTOMER NOTIFICATION DRAFT ---
Hello,

We experienced a service degradation affecting inference throughput for some Hosted API requests in the us-west-2 region earlier today. Our on-call team applied mitigations (limited large concurrent batches, routed traffic to a fallback model, and restarted affected workers) which restored throughput and latency to normal levels.

What happened: sustained high-volume large-batch requests caused worker saturation and queue growth, degrading throughput for other customers in the same pool.

What we did: applied temporary throttling to large batches, routed some traffic to a smaller model variant, restarted the affected worker pool, and primed caches to accelerate recovery.

Current status: service restored; we are monitoring for residual issues.

Next steps: we will follow up with a post-incident summary including root cause analysis and long-term mitigations (changes to routing, throttling rules, and autoscale safeguards).

Estimated impact window: ~30–50 minutes from initial alert.

If you saw errors or degraded performance, please reply and include request IDs / timestamps so we can assist.

We apologize for the disruption.
---

alex: and here's the proposed status page update (short form) to publish now.

--- STATUS PAGE UPDATE ---
Incident: Throughput degradation in us-west-2 (hosted inference)
Start: 2154320000 UTC
Status: Mitigations applied — partial recovery, monitoring
Impact: Increased latency and reduced throughput for a subset of Hosted API customers (heavy batch/embeddings workloads)
Action taken: throttled large batches, routed to fallback models, restarted affected worker group, primed caches
Expected recovery: service restored; monitoring for residual issues over next 30 minutes
---

michael: will add the incident to postmortem queue and assign owner. alex, want to own RCA?

alex: I can own RCA, will coordinate infra + product + CS. Tentative timeline: preliminary RCA in 48 hours, full postmortem in 5 business days.

laura: handing off monitoring and watch for the next 30 mins. @jamie you'll get pager for next shift?

jamie: yes, I'll accept handoff in 25 minutes and keep an eye on pool-7 metrics.

ops-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: mitigations applied, status page update drafted, customer notification drafted, RCA owner assigned (alex). Handoff planned to jamie.

alex: quick follow-ups: 1) add permanent rule to deny extremely large single-batch sizes by default, 2) make autoscale more conservative on hot pools, 3) add route-based throttling telemetry so we can auto-detect new route names.

michael: noted. I'll create the infra tickets and link to the incident thread.

cs-team-bot: CS: we'll queue the customer messages for affected accounts; will personalize for top-tier customers.

laura: closing this thread for active mitigation after handoff. If anything regresses ping @oncall. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT: resolved -> monitoring. Final update will be posted to status page once RCA begins.
